2. The petitioner as plaintiff instituted 4  suit for permanent injunction in the Court of the then Upazila Munsit Katiadi being Other Class Suit No. 322 of 1983 stating, interalia that the entire suit plot measuring 1.08 acres recorded in CS. Plot No. 1454 under. CS. Khatian No. 834/835 corresponding to S.A. Khatian No. 735/748 originally belonged to Mathura Nath Goswami in 16 annas ownership and it was so recorded in the C.S. Khatian while the names of Sashi Bhusan Dey and Satish Chandra ‘Dey  were record therein as adheres. Subsequently said Mathura Nath Goswami removed Sashi Shusan and Satish Chandra from. bargaders in respect of 68 acres of land from the suit plot by western side and brought the land under his .khas possession. The said Mathura Math Goswami thereafter :settled by way of pattan 232 acres of land including .6.8 acres from:the suit plot with his son's wife Tarulata, the mother .of the plaintiff, following Which the plaintiffs mother owned and possessed the same in her own right while Sashi Bushan and Satish Chandra part possessed .40 decimals of the suit plot by the eastern side, Satish Chandra was a peon in a Government office and he migrated to India in 1.947 and he did not come back. Thereafter out of his 3 sons in du Bushan migrated to India 30 years ago while another son used to party business at Mymensingh town and his 3rd son continued as the bargadar under the plaintiffs father and thereafter under the plaintiff in. respect of 40 acres of the suit plot, by the eastern side. Mathura Nath Goswami died leaving behind plaintiffs father as the only heir to succeed him and on his death and on the death of Tarulata the plaintiff became the owner of the suit plot. The S.A. Khatian has been prepared in the names of the plaintiff and his mother Tarulata and the name of Bidhu Bhusan was wrongly recorded in S.A. Khatian in respect of 40. decimals of-the suit plot. The plaintiff on humanitarian consideration has gifted the defendant No. 1.17 acres of land from the suit plot by a registered deed dated: 29.4.1972 and the defendant No. 1 possess the same. One Abdus Satter and others were bargaders under the plaintiff in respect of 68 decimals of land of the suit plot but eventually the plaintiff removed them from, bargadar ship and brought it under his own cultivation. When the said Abdus Satter Was removed from the bargadarship he out of sheer grudge .obtained on 7.6.76 a kabala from Bidhu Bushan in the benami of one Amiruddin in respect Of .20 decimals of land from the suit plot The plaintiff in order to avoid unwanted complications and disturbance posed by the said Persons elected to file a pre-emption case in respect of the said land and got it pre-empted. Excluding the aforesaid 17 Decimals of land gifted to the school the plaintiff has been in continuous and peaceful possession in 90 decimals of land on mutating the same in his own name and on payment of rent to the Government Acquired Estate. The defendants have no right, title and. possession in the suit plot but they illegally threatened the plaintiff with dispossession on 16.4.83 when the plaintiff had no other alternative but to file the suit for permanent injunction with a prayer for restraining the defendants from disturbing the plaintiff with his possession in the suit land. 

 3. The defendants contested the suit by filing a written statement wherein they have denied the material averments made in ,the plaint and contended, inter-alia, that the suit plot be longed to SaShi Bushan Dey and Satish Chandra Dey and Satish Chaudra Dey died childless leaving brother to inherit him and subsequently Sashi died leaving. Sons Indu, Bidhu and Kartick 40 decimals of land of the suit plot has been correctly recorded while remaining portion of the suit plot has been wrongly recorded in the name of Tarulata. In the C.S. Khatian the status of Sashi Shusan and Satish Chandra was recorded as tenants and subsequent Indu Bhusan and Bidhu Bushan by amicable arrangement amongst themselves possessed the suit plot in separate sahams while the plaintiff possessed only 20 decimals of the suit plot. The defendant no. 2 gifted 40 decimals of the suit plot to defendant no. 1 and since then the defendant no. 1 is in possession of the said land by digging a pond thereon. The plaintiff have no title and interest in the suit plot and the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 6. The opposite parties did not file any affidavit in-opposition in this Rule. However, Dr. Rafiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties submits that in a suit for permanent injunction the defendant is perpetually enjoined from the assertion of a right or from the commission of an act which would be contrary to the right of the plaintiff. So it is essential for the plaintiff to show in a suit for permanent injunction that he has some legal right to protect and it is essential to prove prima facie title to the property. The next 'submission made by Dr. Rahman is that the lower appellate court has rightly found that the plaintiff has failed to describe the suit plot adequately in the plaint. The description as given in the schedule of the plaint is insufficient, vague, indefinite and unspecified. To fortify his argument he further submits that along with the plaint no sketch map is appended nor boundary of the suit plot is given in the plaint. He further submits that from a perusal of the plaint: specially paragraph 3,4 and 5 it appears that the plaintiff knew as back as in 1976 that the recorded of right at least with regard to 40 decimals of the suit plot were wrongly recorded in the name of Bidhu Bhushan and Satish and he did not take any steps till filing Of the present suit to rectify the said record of right. He further contends that though a cause of action has been given in the 'plaint but actually by filing the suit the plaintiff indirectly wants to nullify the registered deed dated 8.3.83: It has been registered in favour of defendant No. 2. So- in 'a case like this without filing a suit for cancellation of a registered deed dated 8.3.83 and correcting the record of right filing of a. suit for permanent injunction is in competent-as the plaintiff wants to get a relief in fact for carieellatiori of the registered ' deed dated 8.3.83 in a circuitous way. One of his' other argument is that if the trial court's judgment is maintained it may cause inconvenience and hardship to others in that by the decree of the permanent injunction the record of rights and the registered deed dated 8.3.83 will not the affected and there may be transaction in fact with regard to the suit plot by virtue of those documents by which a bonafide purchaser may suffer for no fault of his and in that view of the matter he submits that the present suit is barred under section 54(e) of the Specific Relief Act. Dr. Rahman relying on the observations made by the court of appeal below argued that there are materials on record to arrive at even from the record, of right that the defendant Vs predecessors were recorded as occupancy riyat in the C.S. Khatian and the fact that at least 40 decimals of the suit plot stands in the name of defendants and there-emption case filed by the plaintiff go to show conclusively that the .plaintiff is a:co-sharer in. the suit plot or suit land and, therefore, the finding of the learned court of appeal below that the plaintiff has failed to prove exclusive possession is bourn out by materials on record. 

 8. In the instant case the plaintiffs case is that he is possessing the suit land by way of a gift and inheritance from his mother and father respectively and in this case it is an admitted fact that the C.S. Khatian stands in the name of grandfather of the plaintiff who was the 16 annas owner of the suit plot. It is asaerted by the plaintiff in the plaint that -he is possessing the suit land since long, some time through bargaders and some time cultivating the land by his own laborers  and recently he came to know that the defendant No. 2 got a deed registered in his name and thereafter he started threatening to dispossess him from the suit plot and as such he filed the present .suit to protect his right by way of restraining the defendants from disturbing with his peaceful possession of the suit land. On the other hand, the case of the defendants is that the suit plot never be, longed to Mothura Nath Goswarni, it be longed to Sashi and Bidhu, Bhushan. They were the real owners of the suit Plot. The C.S. Khatian was wrongly recorded in the name of the predecessor in-interest of the plaintiff and the defendant No. 2 got the suit plot trona his father and uncle by way of purchase and inheritance and thereafter recently had gifted some land to the school defendant No. 1 Except 20 decimals of land rest of 'the suit plot is in possess if the defendants. The predecessor in interest of the plaintiff had no right, title and interest in the suit plot. They were never in possession of the suit plot and Satish and Bhidu Bbushan  were never bargadars. They paid part of the products not as bargaders but as rent. The suit is false. 

 9. In support of their respective cases, each side examined 5 witnesses in their behalf. Plaintiff has examined himself as P.W.1 at the trial court and proved his case, and to prove his possession. he exhibited certain documents namely; exhibit l series, 2 series, 5 series, and the. C.S. Khatian. He has also examined the bargaders as witness through Whom  he used to cultivate the suit land and for the last 5 years the suit land was used by the Sugar Mill fell cultivation of Sugarcane and he, has also examined D.C. of the Sugar Mill as P.W.4 to prove his possession in the suit plot. Here it may be stated that in the plaint the plaintiff has asserted 'not only his possession but also the manner of possession. Similarly, in the written statement the defendants asserted the manner of possession but in evidence they have failed to assert the manner of possession in the suit plot. 

 All of us have failed to find any document in the record as exhibit D and Dl. It appears from the evidence of D.W.I that he has exhibited 3 documents namely exhibit A, B and C. But from the order no. 32 of the trial Court it appears that only two documents namely Exhibit A and B have been exhibited. We also do not find any exhibit C in the record. Be that as it may, there is another finding by the appellate court below to the effect that in the C.S. khatian the name of the predecessor-in-interest of the defendants appeared as occupancy raiyat and that shows that the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiff had no right, title and interest in the suit plot or at least the plaintiff along with defendants are co-sharers in the suit plot. I have examined the C.S. khatian and it appears that in the C.S. khatian the name of Sashi Rhushan and Bidhu Bhushan appeared as bargadars and the remark column is blank and there is not a single word to the effect that they are occupancy raiyat under the landlord of the suit plot. Thus it appears to me that the finding given by the lower appellate court on this point is perverse and is based on no evidence at all. It is absolutely contrary to the materials and evidence on record. Here it may be mentioned that the D.W. I in his examination-in-chief stated that 

 Probably the lower appellate court without scrutinizing the Khatian himself relied on this statement of D.W.1 which is contrary to the document and thereby the appellate court below arrived at an erroneous finding. In this connection it may be mentioned that even if lot argument's sake it is admitted that the plaintiff is a co-sharer in the suit plot then also he is entitled to maintain his possession of the suit plot if he can show that he is in exclusive possession of the suit land. 

 15. The defendant no.2 as D.W.1 asserted that he paid rent of the suit plot to the Government but failed to file any rent recipts in that regard. The evidence of D.Ws. 4 and 5 also lends support to the plaintiffs case with regard to the possession of the suit plot. 1 have already discussed earlier that there is no remark in the C.S. khatian regarding the predecessor in-interest of the defendant no. 2 as occupancy raiyat rather in the C.S. Khatian the predecessors-in-interest of the defendant no. 2 were recorded as bargadar under Mothura Nath Goswami, the owner of the suit plot and that the necessary documents of possession have been filed and exhibited by the plaintiff as exhibit 1 series, 2 series and 5 series. Thus it appears on analysis and scrutiny of the materials and evidence on record that the finding of the lower appellate court that the plaintiff has failed to prove his exclusive possession in the suit plot is perverse and contrary to the materials and evidence on record. He has relied on certain documents namely Ext. D and D1 which are neither exhibited nor found in the record.
